a.text: Those with strength are disposed to be 'hunters'.
Buried in ruins at death's door, awaiting the quiet reaper's call,
this sort of 'truth' is the very first thing one learns.

steps.text: Perhaps my understanding is flawed, but does the handling method Rhodes Island has chosen fall under the... cooperation you mentioned?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Our liaison was precisely to discuss that, but it seems you've arrived a few hours ahead of schedule.
I would imagine that even on dry land, arriving earlier than the designated time ought not undermine trust.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And even in Ægir, traipsing through the entryway of another's home without so much as a greeting ought not constitute etiquette.
You remain quite eloquent, but I have no intention of apologizing. Moreover...
Before the Ægir's voice reaches, she has already reappeared over ten meters away, standing before the door at corridor's end as if she had been there all along.
Only her voice, left to linger in the hallway, attests to her movement.
She presses her lance lightly against the solitary door, covered in pale blue stickers. Her expression communicates both disgust and indignation, yet her breathing is calm and unperturbed.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Forgive me for asking, but what purpose could compel you to allow a room of this kind, Dame Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: As I described in my letter, those living quarters belong to another partner of Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Do I mishear you? It is my solemn hope that you have not been drawing inspiration from that school of lunatics and their revolting technology.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Rest assured that we will not attempt to contend with a menace threatening to engulf this land by making use of a different one.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: That is a relief above any other.
An oblique notch is abruptly slashed into the tough alloy of the doorway, and in one audible movement the Ægir's foot elegantly pries it apart into two clean halves.
She disappears through it, sweeps across the room as if searching, and reappears with nothing to show, all in the blink of an eye.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: How bizarre. I've somehow managed to mistake the scent of those dregs.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Or perhaps I should have realized that when you never lifted a finger to stop me, it was not out of acquiescence.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Setting aside your combat skills, I fear the Abyssal Hunters must also learn to control their emotions when faced with their old enemy.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Although their present evolution is but the fruit of selective pressures, unguided by intellect, there may always come a day when they reach that milestone.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Keh. Assume they do. Perhaps, one day, I will indeed try and resist the urge to mangle those filthy beings just long enough to understand their intent.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Tell me, then. Does Rhodes Island house these things simply to teach me that valuable lesson?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I had no intention of playing games with you. My confidence in the Abyssal Hunters' remarkable drive to action simply meant I couldn't let this conversation end before it began.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: And for whose sake does your firm believe my Hunters so carefully and cautiously interact with you all? Keeping far from the landship, daring not to be wounded or shed blood?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The information we can obtain from the subject's physiology is worth far more than the brutal death of a single Sea Terror. As a designer of warfare yourself, you should understand this.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I've transferred the cooperating subject known as 'Mizuki' elsewhere for the time being. I hope we can now have an even-tempered discussion and reach an equally rational conclusion.

a.text: The 'good' who create and contribute to their race.
The 'bad' who plunder and waste the resources of their race.
Only after leaving the village and encountering a great deal of strangers,
was it slowly realized that individuals drew such a decisive 'difference' between themselves.

steps.text: Several months ago
City of Dossoles, Bolívar

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Alright, looks like the Singas guys took the bait! Quick, tell our men to follow the plan!

steps.name: Cowardly Mercenary
steps.text: Uh, got it.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: When this is all over, our brothers will finally be... truly free!

steps.name: Ernesto
steps.text: The explosion didn't alert Ms. Candela, did it?

steps.name: Bolívarian Serviceman A
steps.text: Reporting in, no. Our informants have been shadowing her the whole time. She's never left the room, and hasn't sent out any instructions.

steps.name: Ernesto
steps.text: Excellent. It's still a few hours until sunrise. That's plenty of time for a cover-up.

steps.name: Ernesto
steps.text: We can't let her catch wind of our explosives. The only thing she won't ignore is anything that risks her city plates getting destroyed and scaring the bastards living it up here.

steps.name: Ernesto
steps.text: Have we found out who was responsible for the warehouse yet?

steps.name: Bolívarian Serviceman B
steps.text: Reporting in, it was two mercenaries from True Bolívarians.

steps.name: Bolívarian Serviceman B
steps.text: But we can't link to their comm terminals, and they're not in their hideout. Our guys are on their trail right now.

steps.name: Ernesto
steps.text: Any moves from the Singas side? With the Championship coming up, they should be asking Ms. Candela what the hell's going on, after their guys got hurt in an explosion.

steps.name: Bolívarian Serviceman B
steps.text: Apparently they're looking for someone. Based on what little we've overheard, they're calling whoever it is 'those kids'.

steps.name: Ernesto
steps.text: Wasn't there a Leithanian youth choir staying at a pub near the warehouse recently?

steps.name: Ernesto
steps.text: Were any of the pub's employees caught in the explosion?

steps.name: Bolívarian Serviceman B
steps.text: Reporting in. We've checked everyone's IDs. Practically all of them were pub security. And simultaneously Singas government soldiers, of course.

steps.name: Ernesto
steps.text: Haha, looks like those two mercenaries got both us and the Singas guys good.

steps.name: Ernesto
steps.text: If the Singas people aren't complaining to Ms. Candela, then maybe they were planning to buy the explosives from them...

steps.name: Ernesto
steps.text: And the True Bolívarians side used the deal as a trap to lure in and blow up the Singases in the pub. Taking the opportunity to kidnap the VIPs too—the 'kids'.

steps.name: Bolívarian Serviceman B
steps.text: What? That takes some balls... What's the plan, then?

steps.name: Ernesto
steps.text: Prioritize staging it to look like a fire, just your everyday accident. Ms. Candela needs to believe that.

steps.name: Ernesto
steps.text: Maybe if we can find the kids first, we'll have even more room to bargain with the Singases...

steps.name: Bolívarian Serviceman A
steps.text: Reporting in! We just intercepted an anonymous message on its way to the police terminals.

steps.name: Bolívarian Serviceman A
steps.text: It's got info on True Bolívarians kidnapping the Leithanian choir, as well as some coordinates.

steps.name: Bolívarian Serviceman A
steps.text: Right now we're the only ones with the tip-off. What's our next move?

steps.name: Ernesto
steps.text: Wipe all traces of it immediately! We can't let Ms. Candela's people find out.

steps.name: Ernesto
steps.text: The coordinates are probably fake. Don't jump the gun. Just seal all routes out of the city, and focus on making it look like a fire.

steps.name: Bolívarian Serviceman A
steps.text: On it!

steps.name: Ernesto
steps.text: What the hell's going on...? Who's behind this? Who would it even benefit?

steps.name: Ernesto
steps.text: ...Who's there?
Shoot, he's really sharp. But he'll have to try a little harder if he wants to find me.
Hm... I can't just ignore it when bad guys are doing bad things to children.
Come to think of it, they arrived from Leithanien on the same merchant ship I was on, only a couple days ago. It's like fate, kinda.
I haven't even heard them sing on the big stage yet. Can't waste the ticket I bought.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Tch. How can a pub have so many guards? We dealt with every last one we drew out, and there were still all those guys left.

steps.name: Cowardly Mercenary
steps.text: But, uh, our brothers more or less dealt with them, so it worked out...

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Hmph, goddamn Singas tools. Why guard those kids with all those men in the middle of the night?

steps.name: Cowardly Mercenary
steps.text: It feels like they're... guarding the kids themselves? Or else their people will run? Weird...

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: You might just be onto something. Could really be what's happening.

steps.name: Cowardly Mercenary
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Think. None of our brothers actually want to get into this random shit with those True Bolívarians, do they? Maybe we're all planning to make a run for it?

steps.name: Cowardly Mercenary
steps.text: Yeah... Yeah, but I always thought Pancho's ideas made some sense...

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Hey. Who gives a shit what makes sense? It can be the biggest no-brainer and it's still useless if he can't take the city with it.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: And well, even if he does, all you can do with this city is skim dirty money off the top. It doesn't even have a single proper workyard.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: He wants to fund the Bolívarian nation? Without support from the Columbians and Leithanians, I doubt he can fund even a single decent weapon.

steps.name: Cowardly Mercenary
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: No buts. Even if there's a way, it's not for us guys under the hood to figure out.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Just listen to me, okay? Once this is over, we're all off to live the good life.
*Sigh*...

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: What are you sighing for?

steps.name: Cowardly Mercenary
steps.text: Huh? Did I make a noise?
Maybe YOU can go live the good life, but who knows where the children you sold will end up?

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Conchetumare, what carajo business is it to you?! Where did you even come from, pendejo? I'll sell you with the rest of 'em!

steps.name: Cowardly Mercenary
steps.text: Yeek!

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: What're you so scared of?

steps.name: Cowardly Mercenary
steps.text: My knife... I was gonna slash him, y'know, show some blood to freak him out, but the knife just kinda rolled up!

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Useless garbage! What'd I just say about these crappy weapons? They wouldn't do shit to a baby.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Also, watch the kid's skin. Soft and smooth sells. No cutting, just follow my lead...

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Urk...

steps.name: Cowardly Mercenary
steps.text: Why are you lying down? Let's catch him... guh? The room's tilting! I can't stand!

steps.name: Cowardly Mercenary
steps.text: Urgh...

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Tch. Pendejo. What goddamn evil shit are you? You got cups on your shoes or something? How are you standing on this steep-ass...
Huh? You're the ones standing crooked to me. Must be why you think everything else is wonky, and you're the only ones standing straight, huh?

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Tch! Who sent you? What kinda Leithanian black magic is this? What the hell are you, kid?!

options: Why do we have to be so on guard?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm very sorry, Dr. {@nickname}, but I still believe it's not yet time to give you the whole explanation.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Full elucidation would only serve to add to your current worries, and therefore impact your judgment in many areas.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Regardless of whether you see yourself as a commander, or as a guide.

options: Not comprehending also adds to my worries.
Having unknown personnel aboard disturbs my judgment.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Which is why I haven't concealed the Medical Department's plans for, and stance towards, the subject. Moreover, we invited you into this discussion as early as possible.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: As for your proposal to exempt the subject from some of the agreed upon restrictions, you will be briefed on the various risks this poses to you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: While it may not address all of your doubts, I would still like for you to listen to the staff and I's opinions at the meeting.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They'll be here soon.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Our brothers will be here soon! Don't get so full of yourself!
I wasn't planning to. But I doubt your friends can make it, because they all went lights out before you did. Just like the guy next to you.
But the kids you took should be waking up right about now.
An underground cellar is no place for a dozen children to be sleeping. They should be at home, in bed.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: You...!

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Tch, listen to yourself. 'Home'.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: What home, huh? What home are they ever gonna have?

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Like hell a spoiled Leithanian brat who dresses like a freak would know how those kids live!
Huh? I'm not Leithanian. My name's 'Mizuki'. Even you can tell that sounds Higashinese, right?

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: Oh, and if we're talking about 'homes', I think I've got a little right to speak, at least.

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: After all, my home was destroyed by bad guys when I was really young. A bunch of criminal scum who robbed others. Just like you, how about that?

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Hff...

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: What the hell do you understand, brat? I-It's not like I wasn't trying to help those kids too!

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: You don't even know why the Singases sent those kids here!

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: So they could perform, duh? Make Bolívarians familiar with Leithanian culture?

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: 'The people here eat, sleep and breathe what the Columbians do, yet all their influence comes from Leithanian culture.'

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: I've been sick of your True Bolívarians pretexts since forever ago.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Heheh, hahahahahah! True Bolívarians...

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: The people who chose this city never identified with Bolívar in the first place. Even if they did, it'd get rubbed outta them sooner or later.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: The people who come here, whether Bolívarian, Columbian, or Leithanian, are all here for goddamn son-of-a-bitch money!

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: You think they're here to watch Leithanian musicals and poems?

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: They're just looking for good performers with nice voices and pretty faces to amuse them at their dinner parties!

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: But the Leithanian bastards knew that from the start. They used these kids as goddamn props to make their goddamn deals.

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: Guess you've got it all figured out.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: I do. How could I not? Our line of business ain't nothing more than fighting in a rich man's world.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: All they gotta do is cough up some cash and we're behind them, babysitting their goddamn pets! Of course we all eventually see through that rotten bullshit.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: And those kids... they're no different.

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: Sure, you're both struggling, but you can't deny that you're using them as tools for your own profit too.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: And these 'children' weren't using the bigshots of Dossoles either? They never exploited them for any goddamn benefit?!

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: Must be nice to still be able to nitpick this stuff while crawling around on the ground. The children never kidnapped anyone to use as chips in their deals.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Wha... What the hell is...? Don't you come any closer!

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Goddamn bastard, why can't I move? You little bitch...

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: And bad guys beyond cure, like you, should just—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: As described in the meeting, he's already become an entirely different form of life, a type of organism that transforms and reconstructs itself to seek a way forward.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I assume you understand that life depends on finite resources for survival. Moreover, these organisms must consume vast quantities to achieve their transformations.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Simply put, they are currently caged by their finite environment, actively reducing their own consumption in order to continue their race. Hibernating beneath the tides.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But there may come a day when we must compete with them, over all that is required to survive.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Just as we hunt the vermin that ruin our village stores, so too will we snatch their lives away. Or, perhaps, we will instead become the nutrients stowed in their folds.

options: If so, you don't need me to choose.
But you still put the choice in front of me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I imagine you've already noticed. Unlike the rest of his kin, the subject has drifted beyond identifying with his race. He has his own thoughts and bewilderments.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If not, we might not be having this discussion at all.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: These creatures' transformations and evolutions were originally meant to propel their race's development.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But perhaps the subject cannot truly be called the same. Not the same as one of those lifeforms, nor as you or I.

steps.name: Choir Member
steps.text: Stop it!

steps.name: Choir Member
steps.text: He's... He's the same as us!

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: H-How did you get here?

steps.name: Choir Member
steps.text: ...I planned all of this.

steps.name: Choir Member
steps.text: I slipped out a few nights ago, and used my singing to transmit mental suggestions with Originium Arts, getting all the dead-drunk Bolívarian mercenaries to take the bait.

steps.name: Choir Member
steps.text: The pub's guards were obsessed with buying the explosives thanks to the information I leaked, too.

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: So, even if I didn't come save you...

steps.name: Choir Member
steps.text: I wrote a message for the police ahead of time, set to send by terminal on a timer.

steps.name: Choir Member
steps.text: If they try him... then I'm an accomplice.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Tch, stupid little choir kid... You trying to sympathize with me? Is this a joke?

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: Man, this is turning into a real headache. I just wanted to get you all back so I wouldn't waste the ticket I ordered for that upcoming music program.

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: So... in this situation, do you still count as a bad guy, mister?

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Heh, cut the bullshit, Leithanian dog. Kill me or whatever, that's up to you.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: But if you Leithanian shits dare touch those kids or snatch them back, then even death ain't gonna stop me from being your worst nightmare!

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: I told you, I wasn't sent by the Leithanians.

steps.name: Choir Member
steps.text: By now, these people must be fed up with life in this city and all the endless fighting.

steps.name: Choir Member
steps.text: I'm so sorry I used them in my own selfish escape plan...

steps.name: Choir Member
steps.text: But maybe they're the same as me... We all just want to escape this city, to escape our own homes.

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: Augh, seriously...?

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: Fine, I'll back off and stop meddling. Otherwise, I'll start to seem like the bad guy.

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: But I don't think your plan would've worked without these people's greed.

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: So just to be safe, I'll let them nap for a little longer, while you guys get away.

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: I'll be watching him.

a.text: but ever since recovering my life, I've always seen myself and others as 'different'.
But if so, who would be 'the same'?
Who would be truly willing to treat me as 'the same'? Or... to become 'the same'?

options: Even if this is all true, I'm still...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I have never called your ability into question, Dr. {@nickname}.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I have complete faith that you can guide his transformation and reconstruction in a direction we would consider 'good'.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But is it appropriate for us to transform a person like this? Simply because we can? Simply because we maintain that one specific form of survival is the proper one?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Is it at all different from altering the subject's personhood in pursuit what we maintain is a finer form of life?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This isn't an interrogation, Dr. {@nickname}. I simply want to know if you've ever had the notion that 'our own form of life is superior'.

options: I'll give him the freedom to choose.
I won't interfere in his way of thinking.
I'll take responsibility for my own conduct.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This may sound somewhat arrogant, but even possessing choice is often a luxury we don't have, let alone bestowing it.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But it is indeed an improvement over interfering with others simply because you can.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mere interaction necessarily gives rise to interference, even if it is not one's intent. Even if it is not through spoken language.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: When you decided you'd treat the subject as an Operator and communicated with him as such, you were already bound to influence one another.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That's the answer I most wanted to hear, yet also the one that most concerns me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The operators trust, love, and respect you, and entrust their lives to you on missions, all because of your willingness to step forth. Because only you can do that.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I have not the slightest doubt that you can bear your ever-increasing responsibilities. But there may come a day when they contradict each other, conflict with each other, and drive you to make an unwilling choice.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: However, as you've resolved yourself to do so, I will not stand in your way.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I often warn the operators you command that, should they approve of you, they ought not harbor too many misgivings about you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Not just because it would hinder effectiveness in combat, and numerous other projects. But because for many people, this place is their home.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Goodbye then, Dr. {@nickname}. Don't keep those who trust you waiting outside for too long.

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: Doctor, Dr. Kal'tsit said I'd be officially under your command starting today!

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: It's a pity I still can't be a formal Operator, but as long as you need my help, I'll do whatever I can.

options: I'll work to get you formal Operator status too.

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: That feels like a kinda half-hearted reply.

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: Are you still chewing over all that complicated stuff? Or am I just worrying too much?

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: What's wrong, Doctor? Something on your mind?

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: Whatever troubles you, you can always talk to me, you know.

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: Huh? Is that what you want?

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: I don't really care what status I have, as long as I'm with you.

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: Speaking of which, you really don't have to worry about me...

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: I agreed to all of Dr. Kal'tsit's strict limitations to protect both my info and my safety.

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: Really, Doctor...

steps.name: Mizuki
steps.text: We're all responsible for our choices, right?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You may be of the mistaken belief that such an argument would produce some kind of... compassion.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Of course not.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your investigation of dry land will sooner or later require support from dry land. And resisting the underwater enemy may also sooner or later become the task of those on dry land.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: So long as you do not interfere with Rhodes Island's singular foray into this field, I can discuss the terms with you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I will exhaust all possibilities in supporting your pursuit of that group's traces on dry land, with our existing intelligence-sharing agreement as the foundation.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: All for the sake of shielding an ignorant individual transformed into an abomination?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: All for the sake of having another possibility in the future.
